title: Identifying Self-Admitted Technical Debts with Jitterbug: A Two-Step Approach

edges.target: Maldonado & Shihab SATD dataset (10 Java projects)
edges.ref: [5] E. d. S. Maldonado and E. Shihab, "Detecting and quantifying different types of self-admitted technical debt," in MTD, 2015.
edges.evidence: the performance of Jitterbug is tested through simulations on a publicly available SATD dataset originally collected by Maldonado and Shihab [5]. This dataset contains ten open-source java projects

edges.target: Maldonado & Shihab SATD ground-truth labels (corrected by this paper)
edges.ref: [5] E. d. S. Maldonado and E. Shihab, "Detecting and quantifying different types of self-admitted technical debt," in MTD, 2015.
edges.evidence: most of the false positives (98%) were wrongly labeled in the original dataset. That means these strong patterns identified by Jitterbug are even more accurate than human experts

edges.target: MAT keyword baseline (Guo et al.)
edges.ref: [6] Z. Guo, S. Liu, J. Liu, Y. Li, L. Chen, H. Lu, Y. Zhou, and B. Xu, "Mat: A simple yet strong baseline for identifying self-admitted technical d...
edges.evidence: MAT: a baseline approach from Guo et al. [6] where a set of human-derived patterns— "todo, fixme, hack, xxx" is applied to find the "easy to find" SATDs.

edges.target: TM text-mining ensemble (Huang et al.)
edges.ref: [32] Q. Huang, E. Shihab, X. Xia, D. Lo, and S. Li, "Identifying self-admitted technical debt in open source projects using text mining," EMSE, 2018.
edges.evidence: TM: ensemble model from Huang et al. [32] where a Multinomial Naive Bayes model is trained on selected features with information gain ... we apply it as a baseline algorithm.

edges.target: Huang et al. reported 73% F1
edges.ref: [32] Q. Huang, E. Shihab, X. Xia, D. Lo, and S. Li, "Identifying self-admitted technical debt in open source projects using text mining," EMSE, 2018.
edges.evidence: By implementing a boosting technique using all those sub-classifiers, they have found an average of 73% F1 scores for all datasets [32].

edges.target: CNN SATD detector (Ren et al.)
edges.ref: [3] X. Ren, Z. Xing, X. Xia, D. Lo, X. Wang, and J. Grundy, "Neural network-based detection of self-admitted technical debt: From performance to ex...
edges.evidence: Due to the difficulty of reproducing a deep learning solution, we used the same precision, recall, F1 scores reported in Ren et al. [3]

edges.target: Ren et al. reported 78% F1 and 3,548 s CNN training time
edges.ref: [3] X. Ren, Z. Xing, X. Xia, D. Lo, X. Wang, and J. Grundy, "Neural network-based detection of self-admitted technical debt: From performance to ex...
edges.evidence: is much lower than training a deep learning model (3,548 seconds for training a CNN model in Ren et al. [3]).

edges.target: Zampetti et al. reported 74% AUC / 55% precision / 57% recall
edges.ref: [4] F. Zampetti, A. Serebrenik, and M. Di Penta, "Automatically learning patterns for self-admitted technical debt removal," in SANER, 2019.
edges.evidence: Even the state-of-the-art machine learning approaches can only reach around 78% F1 score [3] and 74% AUC [4] ... the process cannot be fully automated

edges.target: Maldonado et al. reported 63% F1 with 23% training data
edges.ref: [30] E. d. S. Maldonado, E. Shihab, and N. Tsantalis, "Using natural language processing to automatically detect self-admitted technical debt," TSE,
edges.evidence: Maldonado et al. [30] successfully identified two types of SATD in 10 open-source projects (average 63% F1 Score) using Natural Language Processing

edges.target: FAST2 recall estimator (Yu & Menzies)
edges.ref: [47] Z. Yu and T. Menzies, "Fast2: An intelligent assistant for finding relevant papers," ESA, 2019.
edges.evidence: This estimator, also described in Algorithm 3, is adopted from our previous work [47] where it was shown to outperform any other state-of-the-art estimators.

edges.target: APFD metric (Rothermel et al.)
edges.ref: [51] G. Rothermel, R. H. Untch, C. Chu, and M. J. Harrold, "Prioritizing test cases for regression testing," TSE, 2001.
edges.evidence: APFD: first proposed in test case prioritization [51], APFD calculates the area under the recall-cost curve.

edges.target: Cohen's d small effect size threshold (0.2 x SD)
edges.ref: (no reference entry; "Cohen'd effect size test" applied uncited)
edges.evidence: we applied Cohen'd effect size test to determine which results are similar. To that end, we calculated: Small_step2 = 0.2 · StdDev(All APFD results) = 0.02.

edges.target: scikit-learn
edges.ref: footnote 2: https://scikit-learn.org/
edges.evidence: Implemented with scikit-learn package LogisticRegression in Python with balanced class weight ... DecisionTreeClassifier ... RandomForestClassifier ... SGDClassifier ... MultinomialNB

edges.target: srcML comment extractor
edges.ref: footnote 5: https://www.srcml.org/
edges.evidence: Data collection: we applied srcML and extracted 17,208 code comments from the Apache httpd-2.4.6 project, similar to what Potdar and Shiha [22] did.
edges.section: 6 Apply Jitterbug to A New Project

edges.target: Apache httpd-2.4.6 source (project choice following Potdar & Shihab)
edges.ref: footnote 4: https://archive.apache.org/dist/httpd/httpd-2.4.6.tar.gz; [22] A. Potdar and E. Shihab, ICSME 2014.
edges.evidence: we applied Jitterbug to identify SATDs from a new, unlabeled project Apache httpd-2.4.6
edges.section: 6 Apply Jitterbug to A New Project

edges.target: Potdar & Shihab keyword method result on Apache httpd (112 SATDs)
edges.ref: [22] A. Potdar and E. Shihab, "An exploratory study on self-admitted technical debt," in ICSME, 2014.
edges.evidence: Potdar and Shiha [22] applied their keyword-based method to identify SATDs on Apache httpd-2.4.6. They found 112 SATDs in total. The Jitterbug result is better
edges.section: 6 Apply Jitterbug to A New Project

edges.target: Random forest (Ho) as Hard's internal learner
edges.ref: [44] T. K. Ho, "Random decision forests," in ICDAR, 1995.
edges.evidence: Given that the #Best of random forest is higher, we choose random forest as the internal model of Hard for the rest of the experiments.

edges.target: Logistic regression (Wright)
edges.ref: [42] R. E. Wright, "Logistic regression." 1995.
edges.evidence: LR: logistic regression model described in §3.2. Implemented with scikit-learn package LogisticRegression

edges.target: Decision tree learning (Rokach & Maimon)
edges.ref: [43] L. Rokach and O. Z. Maimon, Data mining with decision trees: theory and applications. World scientific, 2008.
edges.evidence: DT: decision tree model described in §3.2. Implemented with scikit-learn package DecisionTreeClassifier

edges.target: Multinomial Naive Bayes (Rish)
edges.ref: [45] I. Rish, "An empirical study of the naive bayes classifier," in IJCAI 2001 workshop on empirical methods in artificial intelligence, 2001.
edges.evidence: NB: Multinomial Naive Bayes model described in §3.2. Implemented with scikit-learn package MultinomialNB in Python.

edges.target: Soft-margin linear SVM (Suykens & Vandewalle)
edges.ref: [46] J. A. Suykens and J. Vandewalle, "Least squares support vector machine classifiers," Neural processing letters, 1999.
edges.evidence: SVM: linear soft-margin support vector machine model described in §3.2. Implemented with scikit-learn package SGDClassifier

edges.target: jDeodorant comment extractor (used by dataset creators)
edges.ref: [48] M. Fokaefs, N. Tsantalis, E. Stroulia, and A. Chatzigeorgiou, "Jdeodorant: identification and application of extract class refactorings," in I...
edges.evidence: When Maldonado and Shihab [5] created this dataset, jDeodrant [48] was applied, which is an Eclipse plugin for extracting comments from the source code of java files.

edges.target: Alves et al. TD type ontology (labels collapsed to binary)
edges.ref: [49] N. S. Alves, L. F. Ribeiro, V. Caires, T. S. Mendes, and R. O. Spínola, "Towards an ontology of terms on technical debt," in TechDebt, 2014.
edges.evidence: two humans then manually classified each comment according to the six different types of TD mentioned by Alves et al. [49] ... we have changed the final label into a binary problem

edges.target: Cohen's kappa +0.81 agreement on dataset labels
edges.ref: [50] J. Cohen, "Weighted kappa: Nominal scale agreement provision for scaled disagreement or partial credit." Psychological Bulletin, 1968.
edges.evidence: reported a high level of agreement, using Cohen's Kapp [50] coefficient of +0.81 ... indicates that the dataset is unbiased and reliable.

edges.target: Bavota & Russo: SATDs survive over 1,000 commits
edges.ref: [1] G. Bavota and B. Russo, "A large-scale empirical study on self-admitted technical debt," in MSR, 2016.
edges.evidence: even when fixed, it survives long time (over 1,000 commits on average) in the system [1]

edges.target: Wehaibi et al.: TD only 3% of code yet causes future defects
edges.ref: [2] S. Wehaibi, E. Shihab, and L. Guerrouj, "Examining the impact of self-admitted technical debt on software quality," in SANER, 2016.
edges.evidence: the number of technical debts in a project may be very low (only 3% on average), yet they create a significant amount of defects in the future

edges.target: Nugroho et al. (SIG): $857,500 TD, 15% ROI
edges.ref: [9] A. Nugroho, J. Visser, and T. Kuipers, "An empirical model of technical debt and interest," in MTD, 2011.
edges.evidence: a regular mid-level project owes $857,500 in TD and resolving TD has a Return On Investment (ROI) of 15% in seven years.

edges.target: Guo et al.: cost of deferred TD is twice immediate
edges.ref: [8] Y. Guo, C. Seaman, R. Gomes, A. Cavalcanti, G. Tonin, F. Q. Da Silva, A. L. Santos, and C. Siebra, "Tracking technical debt—an exploratory case...
edges.evidence: concluded that the cost of resolving TD in the future is twice as much as resolving immediately.

edges.target: Maldonado et al.: 75% of SATDs removed, median lifetime 18-173 days
edges.ref: [26] E. d. S. Maldonado, R. Abdalkareem, E. Shihab, and A. Serebrenik, "An empirical study on the removal of self-admitted technical debt," in ICSM...
edges.evidence: 75% of SATDs get removed, but the median lifetime of SATDs ranges from 18 to 173 days [26].

edges.target: Validity-threat categories (Feldt & Magazinius)
edges.ref: [52] R. Feldt and A. Magazinius, "Validity threats in empirical software engineering research-an initial survey." in SEKE, 2010.
edges.evidence: There are several validity threats [52] to the design of this study. ... Conclusion validity ... Internal validity ... Construct validity ... External validity

not_reuse_examples: [7] Cunningham 1993 (WyCash) - origin of the term 'technical debt'; historical background only, nothing adopted.
[39] Wattanakriengkrai et al. N-gram IDF and [40] Flisar & Podgorelec word embeddings - named only as future-work directions, not run or compared against.
[29] Sierra et al. SATD survey and [33]-[38] comment-quality studies (iComment, tComment, Steidl, Malik, Fluri) - related-work narrative, no method, data or number reused.
[41] Siva dzone article - generic definition of pattern recognition vs machine learning; no procedure adopted.
notes: Empirical/method paper (Jitterbug = Easy pattern miner + Hard active learner); self-corrects 434 labels of the reused Maldonado-Shihab dataset (98% of Easy's 'false positives' were mislabels); CNN [3] compared only via reported numbers; Cohen's d threshold applied without citation; intro says 74% AUC for [4] while related work says 0.73.
